resale_co.name: Resale CCO Application ('Sale Application for Residential Real Estate'), combined with the smoke alarm, carbon monoxide alarm and fire extinguisher certificate
resale_co.issued_by: Point Pleasant Beach Building Department / Fire Official
requirements: Separate application for each unit (for example each side of a duplex)
The owner, agent or other listed party must be present at the inspection
The application asks for the number of open permits on the property

Smoke alarm on each level; type depends on the year built: before 1977, battery alarms (10-year sealed battery since January 1, 2019) in the hall by the bedrooms and on each level including the basement; 1977-1980, AC alarm in the hall by the bedrooms and battery alarms elsewhere; 1981-1983, interconnected AC alarms in the hall by the bedrooms and the basement; 1984-1990, interconnected AC alarms on all levels; 1991 and later, interconnected AC alarms in all bedrooms, the hall by the bedrooms and all levels (battery backup from 1992)
Carbon monoxide alarm in the common hall outside, but within 10 feet of, the bedroom doors; battery, hardwired or plug-in (not needed if no fuel-burning device and no attached garage)
Homes with a monitored NFPA 72 fire alarm system instead of AC alarms need an inspection and certificate of compliance from a certified alarm contractor or electrician

fees.label: Resale CCO application per unit, which is the smoke/CO/extinguisher certificate application (paid once, not a second fee)

resale_co.how_to_apply: Apply online through the Borough's GovPilot 'Sale Application for Residential Real Estate' (CCO Application), one application per unit, with the estimated closing date, owner, buyer and agent details and the contact for scheduling. Online applications are paid by credit card only; the form also offers pay later by cash, check or money order. Building Department, 416 New Jersey Avenue, 732-899-3306, Monday to Friday 9 am to 4 pm.
resale_co.contact_title: Construction Official, Fire Official, Code Enforcement Officer, Fire Subcode Official

resale_co.notes: The Borough's online 'Sale Application for Residential Real Estate' is titled a CCO (Certificate of Continued Occupancy) application for resale of residential properties, but its fee and certification text are those of the state Certificate of Smoke Alarm, Carbon Monoxide Alarm and Portable Fire Extinguisher Compliance, so the resale CCO and the fire certificate appear to be one application and one $90.00 fee per unit. No separate resale housing checklist or other resale fee was found. A search lead points to a Borough ordinance (ecode360, Ord. No. 01-14, adopted 2-27-2001) requiring a 'property transfer certificate' from the Construction Official before a sale of residential property with fewer than three units, but ecode360 could not be opened and no snippet showing the exact words was available, so it is not used as evidence. Rentals need a separate rental certificate of occupancy (online, $100 re-inspection or missed-inspection fee) and are rental-only; short-term rentals under a month are prohibited from September 30 to May 15. The Borough website moved from pointpleasantbeach.org to pointpleasantbeach.gov (old links redirect).

requirements: Smoke alarm on each level; type depends on the year built: before 1977, battery alarms (10-year sealed battery since January 1, 2019) in the hall by the bedrooms and on each level including the basement; 1977-1980, AC alarm in the hall by the bedrooms and battery alarms elsewhere; 1981-1983, interconnected AC alarms in the hall by the bedrooms and the basement; 1984-1990, interconnected AC alarms on all levels; 1991 and later, interconnected AC alarms in all bedrooms, the hall by the bedrooms and all levels (battery backup from 1992)
Carbon monoxide alarm in the common hall outside, but within 10 feet of, the bedroom doors; battery, hardwired or plug-in (not needed if no fuel-burning device and no attached garage)
Homes with a monitored NFPA 72 fire alarm system instead of AC alarms need an inspection and certificate of compliance from a certified alarm contractor or electrician

The Borough application still lists a portable fire extinguisher: 2A-10B:C, no more than 10 lbs, within 10 feet of the kitchen in the path of egress, on the maker's bracket, top no more than 5 feet above the floor, with the owner's manual left for the buyer, serviced within 12 months or with a purchase receipt (state law P.L.2025, c.19 removed the extinguisher from the state requirement)

fire_cert.notes: Point Pleasant Beach is municipally enforced (registry code M); the Borough Fire Official, Brian Martin, also serves as Construction Official. The fee is a flat $90.00 per unit with a $50.00 re-inspection; no lead-time tiers are shown. The Fire Department page gives the Fire Official's phone as 732-899-3306 (the Building Department line); the staff directory gives 732-892-1118, ext. 224 and bmartin@pointpleasantbeach.gov. The DCA fire directory (survey 5/30/2025) lists the older email bmartin@pointbeach.org and (732) 892-1118. The application still requires a fire extinguisher and does not mention the 2025 secondary power source label; P.L.2025, c.19 changed both. The Rental Properties page asks renters to email building@pointbeach.org and call Patty Harth at 732-892-1118, ext. 236.

open_questions: Is the $90.00 GovPilot CCO/smoke application the only Borough requirement for a resale, or is there a separate property transfer certificate or resale inspection by the Construction Official with its own fee?
How many days before closing to apply, and how long the certificate is valid (not shown).
Whether the Borough still requires a fire extinguisher and now checks the secondary power source label.
